Job Title
Senior Manager, KYC Risk & Assurance
Job Description
Senior Manager, KYC Risk & Assurance
KYC & Client Onboarding | Permanent, Full-time | London (UK)
Who are we?
IG is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses. The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next. Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
What's the role?
This is a senior leadership role within KYC and Client Onboarding, reporting to the Head of KYC. You will lead our new KYC Risk & Assurance function, the pillar that gives first line real depth of financial crime expertise, quality oversight and risk decisioning.
Grounded in strong financial crime and compliance knowledge but operational and strategic in outlook, you will lead a team of three: two Enhanced Due Diligence Specialists who handle the most complex institutional and high-risk cases, and a KYC Excellence Manager responsible for process excellence and governance. Through them you will own first-line quality assurance over onboarding, the leadership of EDD and escalation decisioning, and continuous improvement across the KYC lifecycle.
As IG grows its institutional business and continues to uplift its financial crime framework, this role exists to build genuine financial crime capability within first line: making confident, well-reasoned risk decisions at pace, providing credible assurance to senior management on the quality of onboarding, and operationalising the standards and methodologies set by second-line Compliance. You will work in close partnership with, but independently of, second-line Compliance and Financial Crime, keeping the roles of the two lines clear.
What will you do?
Quality oversight and assurance
• Design, own and run a risk-based quality assurance framework over onboarding and EDD, assessing the quality and accuracy of risk assessments and decisions rather than only the completeness of files.
• Provide credible, independent first-line assurance to the Head of KYC and senior management on how effectively onboarding controls are operating.
• Own AML-focused management information and quality reporting into governance committees, giving senior management a clear, evidenced view of financial crime risk and control effectiveness.
EDD leadership and risk decisioning
• Lead the two EDD Specialists in delivering holistic due diligence and approvals on Prime and other high-risk clients to a consistently high standard.
• Act as the empowered senior first-line decision-maker on complex, novel or borderline cases, making well-documented risk decisions at pace and escalating to second line only where genuinely warranted.
• Own clear escalation pathways and turnaround standards for complex onboarding queries, so that decisions are timely and the client experience is protected.
Framework operationalisation
• Translate the KYC Standards and CRA methodology set by second-line Compliance into effective first-line procedures, checklists, training and business-as-usual practice.
• Lead the rollout and embedding of the KYC refresh process, covering both periodic and event-driven reviews.
• Oversee the risk-based remediation of the existing high-risk client population, prioritising the highest-risk clients first.
Process excellence and governance
• Own KYC process excellence and governance across the onboarding lifecycle, supported by the KYC Excellence Manager, driving efficiency and consistency alongside quality.
• Maintain strong standards for document and control governance, record keeping, and the minuting of key forums and committees, so that a clear and auditable trail of decisions is kept.
• Identify and lead improvements to onboarding processes, systems and controls as the business grows and regulation evolves.
Leadership and stakeholder management
• Lead, develop and grow a high-performing team of three across the UK and Poland.
• Build strong, collaborative relationships with the institutional onboarding team, Prime sales, second-line Compliance and Financial Crime, and senior stakeholders across the business.
• Partner with second-line Compliance on the design of KYC Standards and CRA methodology, contributing first-line operational insight while keeping ownership of the standards with second line.
What will you need for this role?
To succeed in this role, we think you'll need:
Experience & Education
• 10 or more years of financial crime and AML experience in financial services, with deep expertise across KYC, CDD and EDD and strong knowledge of the UK MLRs and JMLSG Guidance.
• Proven leadership of financial crime operations, KYC, or quality and assurance teams, including developing people and building capability.
• Demonstrable experience designing and running quality assurance or assurance frameworks over KYC and onboarding.
• Experience operationalising KYC standards, CRA methodologies and refresh processes into day-to-day practice.
• A track record of building AML management information and engaging governance committees and senior stakeholders.
• Good working understanding of the FCA regulatory environment. Bachelor's degree in Law, Business, Finance, Economics or a related field, and a recognised AML qualification (for example the ICA Diploma or ACAMS) is desirable.
Personal Attributes
• Acts with integrity and consistently demonstrates high professional and ethical standards.
• Combines operational delivery with strategic thinking, and is pragmatic and commercial in how they enable growth while protecting the firm.
• Exercises senior judgement with credibility and gravitas, and provides confident, effective challenge.
• A strong people leader who builds, develops and motivates high-performing teams.
• Communicates clearly and influences effectively at senior levels.
• Comfortable operating across the first and second line boundary while keeping the roles distinct.
• Demonstrates resilience and a strong sense of delivery and accountability.
• Comfortable working from IG's London office a minimum of three days per week.

Waste Operative
Location: Filton, Bristol
Hours: Monday to Friday, 06:00 – 14:30
Contract Type: Permanent
About the Role
We are seeking a resolute and safety-conscious Waste Operative to join our waste management team. This is a vital role supporting the efficient collection, segregation, and disposal of both hazardous and non-hazardous waste streams across our site operations.
Working closely with the Waste Team Leader and on-site Supervisor, you will play a key part in ensuring our site maintains the highest standards of waste management, environmental compliance, and workplace safety.
What your day to day will look like
Waste Collection and Management You will be responsible for the safe collection and transportation of various waste streams from multiple locations around the site. This includes managing both hazardous materials (including IBCs and drums) and non-hazardous waste, ensuring correct segregation and handling procedures are followed.
Transportation and Logistics Operating a flatbed vehicle, you will transport collected waste materials to the designated waste yard. All movements must be conducted safely, efficiently, and in compliance with site traffic management procedures and relevant transport regulations.
Waste Yard Operations Within the waste yard, you will prepare waste materials for collection by licensed contractors. This includes organizing, labelling, and staging waste according to regulatory requirements and contractor specifications, ensuring all documentation is accurate and complete.
Equipment Operation You will operate a counterbalance forklift truck to move, stack, and organize waste containers and materials. Safe operation and daily equipment checks are essential aspects of this responsibility.
Team Collaboration Working as an integral member of the waste team, you will communicate effectively with colleagues, supervisors, and contractors to ensure smooth operations and timely waste removal. You will support team objectives and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.
Health, Safety, and Compliance Maintaining strict adherence to health and safety protocols is paramount. You will follow all site-specific procedures for handling hazardous materials, wear appropriate personal protective equipment, and report any incidents, near-misses, or equipment defects immediately.
Essential Requirements
Licenses and Certifications A full UK driving license is essential for this role, as you will be driving site vehicles daily. A valid counterbalance forklift truck license is required. Both licenses must be in date and free from restrictions that would prevent operation of required vehicles and equipment.
Experience and Knowledge Previous experience in handling both hazardous and non-hazardous waste streams is highly desirable. Familiarity with waste segregation principles, environmental regulations, and safe handling procedures will be advantageous. Experience working in industrial, manufacturing, or facilities management environments is beneficial.
Skills and Attributes
You must be safety-focused with strong diligence, ensuring compliance with all operational procedures. Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a team are essential. Physical fitness is required, as the role involves manual handling, working outdoors in various weather conditions, and maintaining alertness during early morning starts.
Availability
You must be available to work the fixed shift pattern of 06:00 to 14:30, Monday to Friday, and be dependable and punctual in attendance.

We support each other's wellbeing and champion inclusivity and belonging across teams. What sets JLL apart is our culture of collaboration, both locally in the UK and across the globe. Join us in taking the more inspiring, innovative, and optimistic path on our journey toward success as a Waste Operative in Filton, Bristol.
Note: This role involves working with hazardous materials and requires strict adherence to health and safety procedures.

Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to make an impact and gain hands-on experience working on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for summer placement students who want to be part of something extraordinary —shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
Our placements are designed to help you apply your studies in a practical setting, develop your technical skills, and gain valuable insight into how our business operates.
Our Summer Placement Programme
Our 13 weeks Summer Placement Programme gives you the chance to work in the Materials Testing Laboratory; a lab that supports the production of our world leading radar and electro-optic products. Working under the guidance of experienced Material Engineers, you will be introduced to state-of-the-art methods, technology and equipment used to characterise materials and analyse failures. You will explore all aspects of the materials test lifecycle, which may include requirements analysis, design of samples, implementation of new processes, sample testing, and product support.
Throughout your placement, you’ll receive coaching and support from a dedicated team, with the potential to return for future placements or progress onto our Graduate Development Programme.
The programme will run from 01/06/2027 to 27/08/2027.
We expect you on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience with the laboratory equipment.
As a Summer Placement Materials Engineer you will:
• Be immersed in a busy materials laboratory environment, gaining practical experience across a wide range of material characterisation and testing activities that support critical engineering programmes. You will contribute directly to cutting-edge failure analysis on various materials, components and hardware. Including, additively manufactured metallic materials; where you will help to develop sample preparation techniques and document new laboratory processes.
• Gain a broader understanding of the Materials & Processes Department; working alongside experienced engineers and scientists to see how materials engineering influences the performance, safety and reliability of advanced aerospace systems.
• Have the chance to gain a wider knowledge of the business through various awareness sessions.
• Be given responsibility for delivering a specific project task, providing an excellent opportunity to develop your technical, project management and soft skills.
What you’ll bring
• Be enrolled on a Bachelor’s/Integrated Masters degree from an accredited degree course.
• Relevant engineering or science work experience, such as summer placements or internships.
• Experience with technical writing and project planning.
• Strong analytical, modelling skills and laboratory skills.
• Evidence of successfully working in a team.
• Experience of working in a laboratory and following laboratory procedures is desirable.
For the Summer Placement Materials Engineer role, the acceptable degree programmes are typically:
• Engineering Materials
• Materials Science
• Mechanical Engineering
• Chemical Engineering
• Aerospace Engineering/Manufacturing/Technology
• Physics
• Applied Physics
• Engineering Physics
• Engineering Management
This is not an exhaustive list, and we are keen to hear from you even if you might not have experience in all the above. The most important skill is a good attitude and willingness to learn.
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security requirements and, where applicable, export control restrictions arising from UK Government requirements and customer obligations many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports your wellbeing, learning and development, and work–life balance:

Strategy & Consumer Experience

Our Loyalty division is home to Avios, the global loyalty currency, enabling millions of members to collect and spend rewards across travel, retail and financial services.
Our Holidays division including British Airways Holidays and Iberia Vacaciones, brings together trusted brands, connecting customers to thousands of destinations worldwide through seamless, end-to-end travel experiences.
We’re on an exciting journey of growth and transformation – we’re going places.
The opportunity ✨
If you're looking for a role where you can develop your analytical skills, work on interesting commercial challenges and be part of a supportive team, this could be the perfect next step.
We're looking for two Pricing Executives to join our collaborative Pricing team. One permanent opportunity and one 12-month fixed-term contract.
You'll use data to answer commercial questions and help shape the way customers use Avios. Avios helps millions of people turn everyday spending and travel into rewarding experiences by allowing them to collect and spend points on flights, upgrades, holidays and more. By analysing customer behaviour, demand, redemption trends and pricing performance, you'll uncover insights that help inform pricing decisions, customer propositions and promotions across our Loyalty business.
You'll work with some of the world's best-known airlines on a wide variety of projects, from reward flights and pricing initiatives to new customer propositions. It's a role where you'll see how your analysis helps inform decisions that millions of customers experience.
You'll also be joining a genuinely collaborative team. You'll work closely with experienced analysts, sharing ideas, solving problems together and learning from one another every day. At the same time, you'll be trusted to take ownership of your own work, giving you the opportunity to build confidence while developing your technical and commercial skills.
There are lots of places you could continue your career in analytics. This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others.
You don't need experience in the travel or loyalty industry. If you're excited by the idea of using data to solve real business problems and want to continue developing your analytical skills, we'd love to hear from you.
This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others.
What you'll be doing 🚀
•
Support the development and optimisation of pricing strategies across Reward Flights, Pay with Avios and related loyalty redemption products.
•
Write and optimise SQL queries to explore and combine data from multiple sources.
•
Analyse data using tools including Tableau, Astrato and Excel to identify trends, opportunities and answer commercial questions.
•
Build, own and maintain reports and dashboards, along with presentations that bring data to life to inform tactical and strategic pricing decisions.
•
You’ll play a key role in ensuring our pricing approaches are data-driven, efficient and aligned to business targets.
•
Work closely with colleagues across Commercial, Marketing, Finance, Data and Revenue Management, as well as airline partners.
•
Explore how AI can support more effective and efficient ways of working.
What we need from you ⚡
You'll be someone who has:
•
Proficiency in SQL for data extraction, analysis and reporting through education or a previous role.
•
Strong analytical, numerical and commercial acumen.
•
Experience working with large datasets from multiple sources.
•
High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data accuracy and integrity.
•
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex data clearly and confidently.
•
Experience working with dashboards and reporting tools (e.g. Tableau, Power BI or similar).
•
Confidence engaging with stakeholders at different levels, including senior audiences.
•
An innovative mindset with curiosity, urgency and a desire to continuously improve ways of working.
•
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and take ownership of deliverables.
•
Collaborative approach with strong relationship-building skills across teams.
•
Is curious about AI and interested in how it can support analysis.
The Blend 📍
This role is based in our London office in our Loyalty division.
We call our approach to hybrid working The Blend—it's about giving you the flexibility to choose where you do your best work while staying connected with your team and the wider business.
You'll spend at least two days each week in the office, with the rest of your time working from home. Depending on your role and priorities, you may also work from one of our other offices or partner locations.

You prefer a role with the same routine every day or enjoy working independently with limited collaboration. Location: London
Position: Full time, permanent
The Senior Underwriter - Marine and Energy Liabilities is responsible for underwriting and developing a portfolio of marine and energy liability business, contributing to the profitable growth of an established and well performing account.
The book wrote around 81 million last year with 95% retention, of which around 23 million is led and 57 million followed. It has broadened well beyond its traditional upstream base, with significant growth in power and utilities, and continues to develop as the energy market itself changes.
The team runs as one, rather than as separate marine and energy silos, and is supported by a specialist marine and energy claims function and by the financial security of Mitsui Sumitomo. For an underwriter, that combination means a genuine lead book, a broad appetite and the backing to write meaningful lines.
About The Job
While there is rarely a typical day, here’s a snapshot of some of the key parts of the job:
•
Underwrite and manage a portfolio of marine and energy liability risks, making sound long term decisions within the agreed appetite and authority.
•
Contribute to the lead book, taking underwriting positions the market follows.
•
Proactively develop and pursue new business opportunities, clients and products.
•
Build and maintain strong relationships with brokers and trading partners, representing the syndicate at market meetings and events.
•
Structure solutions that balance client need with profitability, and negotiate terms with confidence.
•
Monitor portfolio performance, identifying trends in pricing, claims and emerging risk, and contribute to portfolio reviews.
•
Support the continued development of the account as the energy market shifts, including the growth we are seeing in power and utilities.

Work closely with our marine and energy claims colleagues so that the claims proposition forms part of what we offer clients.

Analyse and write risks in accordance with our appetite and guidelines, making sound, profitable long term decisions.
•
Understand and negotiate wordings in line with corporate standards.
•
Undertake analysis of the portfolio to identify business opportunities, products and clients, building a robust business case for each.
•
Drive the client experience through oversight of issues raised, including product design, liaison and claims management.
•
Act as a peer reviewer on risks and material endorsements as required.
•
Play an active role in regular underwriting meetings and ensure the risk entry system is maintained.
•
Produce accurate class reports, review underwriting figures regularly so that unusual trends or adverse movements are dealt with, and monitor premium payments.
•
Remain alert to developments affecting the class, its profitability and its opportunities, reporting to leadership as appropriate.
•
Maintain underwriting documentation and records to a high standard.
In addition to your key responsibilities, you will be expected to:
•
Underwrite within your agreed authority, syndicate policies and regulatory requirements, maintaining high standards of governance.
•
Conduct your role in accordance with the company's Business Ethics policy and ensure compliance with relevant risk, regulatory and legal requirements.
•
Effectively represent yourself and the class in external activities, groups and committees.
•
Share market intelligence and technical knowledge across the underwriting team.
•
Contribute to wordings and product development.
•
Act as a referral point and support the development of less experienced colleagues.
•
Act as an ambassador of our company, raising our profile in the market and proactively strengthening our reputation.
•
Build long lasting trusted relationships, developing client insight and ensuring fair outcomes.
•
Abide by MS Amlin's Conduct Rules and Values.
What You’ll Need
Experience:
•
Marine or energy liability underwriting experience gained in the London market.
•
Experience of leading business, or the technical depth and confidence to move into a lead role.
•
A track record of writing new business and developing broker relationships.
•
Sound technical judgement and the ability to make decisions under time pressure.
•
Strong negotiating, networking and relationship building skills.
•
A good understanding of relevant risk, regulatory and legal requirements.
•
ACII or a similar professional qualification would be advantageous.

Are you an NMC Registered Renal trained Nurse looking to take your next career steps with the world’s largest provider of dialysis products and services?
If you are committed to delivering patient-orientated, high-quality care and you have the expertise to maximise efficiency and co-ordinate services, we have an opportunity for you!
What does the role involve?
In a modern, well-equipped environment with a multi-disciplinary approach to care, you will champion best practice in patient management and ensure that Clinic staff are recruited, supported and appraised appropriately. Participating in budget planning, monitoring supplies and maintaining Quality Management Systems, you will play an important role in ensuring the clinic is compliant with standards and performing effectively.
We are looking for a NMC Registered Nurse with solid post-registration experience which includes significant exposure to haemodialysis and outstanding administrative, organisational and clinical skills.  Additionally, you will also have experience of managing others, counselling patients and understanding the role of the Care Quality Commission.
Making a difference to patient’s lives is why we’re here.  As a world leader in renal care, Fresenius offers dedicated, patient centred environments where quality care and the latest technology provide a supportive, modern patient experience.
Bodmin Dialysis Unit operates 14 haemodialysis stations, serving up to 56 patients.
This is a FULL time role of 37.5 hours a week. Current days are working various shifts between 06.30am and 18.00pm Monday to Saturday.
What can we offer you?
Here at Fresenius Medical Care we provide excellent and continuous Training and Development throughout your career, supported by dedicated Clinical Teachers.  On joining, you will enrol on our 8 week Fundamental Dialysis Programme, which is accredited by the European Dialysis and Transplant Nurses Association/European Renal Care Association.  Thereafter, we continue to provide training and education opportunities which significantly exceed the CPD hours required for NMC revalidation, and help take your career to the next level.
We offer a competitive salary UP TO £49,650 - Progression through the pay scale will be underpinned by a Knowledge and Skills Framework (KSF) for each role, allowing employees greater career development potential, aligned to in-house training programmes.
Alongside this we offer a wealth of other fantastic benefits listed below:
•           No Sunday or Night Shift Working
•           Company Pension Scheme and Life Assurance
•           33 Days Holiday (inclusive of 8 days bank holiday) increasing with service
•           Christmas Day and New Year’s Day off
•           Overtime (time and a half after completing full-time hours – 150 hours every 4 weeks)
•           Paid Breaks
•           Free Parking, Uniform, Tea & Coffee, Flu Vaccine and Christmas Meal
•           Health Shield – Company paid Health Cash Plan
•           Long Service Vouchers
•           Refer a Friend Scheme (STAFF NURSE ONLY £1000 per referral if successful)
•           Sick Pay
•           Cycle to Work Scheme
•           Sponsorship for training where applicable for career development
•           bhsf RISE - our Health and Wellbeing hub with 24/7 access to GP’s and Counsellors
•           Blue Light Card - discounts online and in-store.
Who is Fresenius Medical Care?
We are the leading provider of dialysis services to the NHS, operating 52 partnership dialysis units that together provide regular dialysis treatment to over 3,800 NHS patients in the UK.  We are part of a global company treating over 344,000 patients worldwide across over 4,100 clinics.
We also operate 42 production sites on all continents to provide dialysis products such as dialysis machines, dialysers and related disposables. 1 in every 2 of all dialysis machines used around the globe are manufactured by Fresenius Medical Care and we are the 3rd largest medical devices company in the world.
For more information please visit Fresenius Medical Care’s provider website:  www.nephrocare.co.uk
We are a growing and ambitious company who invests in talent and creates an environment where you can grow too.  Come on our journey with us, see your skills develop and be rewarded for the exceptional care you give!
Clinic Manager posts will be subject to an (an enhanced DBS Disclosure)
Fresenius Medical Care is an equal opportunities employer

Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer
Locations: DD, PH, TD, IV, KY and DG
Are you a qualified Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer looking for excellent earning potential, structured work and the security of working directly for an established energy supplier?
At Utilita, we're growing our award-winning Field Services team. Join one of the UK's fastest-growing energy suppliers and a business that has been recognised as one of the UK's Top 50 Best Workplaces for four consecutive years.
What is in it for you?
You'll receive a base salary of £38,993, alongside uncapped earning potential and a variety of opportunities to boost your overall earnings, including:
• On-call payment: Receive £330 for each on-call week, based on an average rota of one week in five. (OTE of £42,293 just with the base salary and conducting mandatory on call requirements)
• Industry-leading installation bonus: Benefit from an uncapped installation bonus of £25 per meter or £50 per dual installation once you have completed a minimum of four installations in a day, with additional work opportunities available to further enhance your earnings.
• London weighting: Receive an additional £2,000 annual allowance if you live within the M25.
• Enhanced overtime: Enhanced overtime rates for Sunday working.
Alongside your salary and uncapped earning potential, you will receive 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, a healthcare scheme, mental wellbeing support, access to 24/7 GP and counselling services, and a generous pension scheme. You will also receive one paid volunteering day each year and have opportunities to win tickets to events at Utilita-sponsored arenas and football matches.
Why work at Utilita?
A schedule that supports your work-life balance.
We understand that a great Smart Meter Engineer role is not just about salary. It is also about having a structured working day and being able to plan your life accordingly.
You will be scheduled an average of 4 jobs per day, with an average travel time to jobs of approximately 35 minutes between appointments.
We aim to schedule your work several weeks in advance, giving you greater visibility of your schedule. This helps you plan life outside work while still giving you the opportunity to take on additional work when it suits you.
First-class training and support.
Your journey will begin at our award-winning training academy in Warrington, where you will receive a comprehensive induction.
You will then receive ongoing mentoring to help you strengthen your knowledge, understand our processes and confidently adapt to the Utilita way of working.
A team that keeps you connected.
We understand that working in the field can sometimes feel isolating, which is why creating a connected and supportive environment is so important to us.
Through regular manager check-ins, access to technical experts, collaborative colleague networks and ongoing communication, you'll always have the support you need and someone to turn to throughout your working day.
What you will be doing.
As a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer, you will represent Utilita in customers’ homes, installing smart meters safely and professionally across domestic properties.
You will play an important role in delivering our customer-first approach, providing a positive experience while maintaining high standards of safety, quality and service.
What we need from you.
To be considered for this opportunity, you will need:
• Smart Metering qualifications, including CCN1 or CMA1 and MET1, or equivalent.
• At least 12 months experience working as a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer.
• A valid full UK driving licence.
Who are Utilita?
Founded in 2003, Utilita Energy was created to challenge the Big Six energy suppliers by offering a fair and flexible service that is good for both the pocket and the planet.
As the first supplier to install a Smart Meter back in 2005 and kick-start Britain’s smart meter revolution, we continue to invest in smart technology and look for new ways to improve our services through innovation.
We are also committed to sustainability, with an ambition to become a Net Zero business by 2030. We believe everyone can make a meaningful impact through small, positive changes.
Our values are simple but powerful:
Fairness. Smart. Sustainability.
Our employees and customers come from all walks of life. We are committed to championing diversity, creating an inclusive culture and providing an environment where you can be your authentic self.
Utilita is part of the Luxion group which comprises Luxion Group Ltd, Utilita Energy Ltd, Luxion Sales Ltd, Utilita Field Services Ltd, Procode Technology Ltd and Canary Care Global Ltd.

Job Description:
At Remitly, we believe everyone deserves the freedom to access, move, and manage their money wherever life takes them. Since 2011, we've tirelessly delivered on our promise to customers sending money globally, providing secure, simple, and reliable ways to manage their money, ensuring true peace of mind. Whether it's supporting loved ones back home, growing a business across continents, or pursuing new opportunities abroad, we're not just here to move money— we're here to move our global customers forward.
We're looking for builders, reimaginers, and global thinkers who want to work at the intersection of technology, trust, and transformation. If that's you and you're ready to do the most meaningful work of your career—we invite you to join over 2,800 passionate Remitlians worldwide who are united by our vision to transform lives with trusted financial services that transcend borders.
About the Role:
The Treasury team manages Remitly's global funding operations — optimising liquidity positions, managing funding corridors, and ensuring capital is available wherever it's needed. Reporting to the Head of Treasury Analytics & Data Science (London), this London-based (hybrid) role sits at the intersection of LLMs, Treasury operations, and data infrastructure.
We're looking for a builder who moves fast from idea to production — someone who can own agentic systems end-to-end and directly increase the operational capacity of the Treasury team.
You Will Build:
Treasury Agent Automation
• Cash flow monitoring agents: intraday cash position tracking, reconciliation, variance flagging, and automated daily reports across accounts and currencies.
• Funding execution agents: instruction routing, approval workflows, payment scheduling, cut-off monitoring, and settlement tracking — encoded with business rules and risk parameters.
• Narrative agents: auto-generated end-of-day and intraday funding commentary, exception summaries, and context-aware alerts delivered to the right stakeholders.
• Discovery-to-deployment pipeline: structured sessions with Funding operators to identify manual tasks, then ship agents that eliminate them — reporting packs, utilisation dashboards, liquidity summaries.
• Embed within the Funding team at the outset — running existing workflows end-to-end alongside operators to develop a first-hand understanding of day-to-day processes, limitations, and pain points before a single agent is scoped or built.
Agent Infrastructure & Growth
• Build reusable, modular agent components and tool libraries that scale as Remitly expands into new markets and corridors.
• Contribute to Treasury-wide agent governance standards, evaluation frameworks, and shared infrastructure.
• Research and recommend emerging LLM capabilities and agentic tooling to keep the Funding function ahead of the curve.
• Partner closely with the Treasury Engineering team to develop the data accuracy, completeness, and timeliness required by Treasury Agents
You Have:
• Advanced proficiency with coding agents across complex development scenarios
• Experience architecting multi-service systems, including complex persistence, integrations, and scaling
• Understanding of distributed systems tradeoffs and cloud-based infrastructure design
• AI tool fluency: orchestrators, automated workflows, comprehensive evaluation pipelines
• Advanced systems architecture expertise across the full technology stack
• Proficiency in customer discovery techniques and ability to connect technical work to business outcomes
• Competence with design thinking, analytics tools, and funnel analysis
• Experience guiding others on AI-first development approaches
• Expertise in experiment modelling, funnel analysis, and data-informed decision making
• Track record of mentoring others and elevating team capabilities
Nice to Have:
• Treasury, fintech, or payments domain knowledge (cash positioning, FX, liquidity).
• LLM observability tools: LangSmith, Arize, Weights & Biases.
• AWS (S3, Glue, Redshift, Lambda); TMS/financial data providers (Bloomberg, Kyriba).
• Startup, founder, or cross-functional multi-product experience.
Our Benefits:
• Paid Vacation Days
• Health insurance
• Commuter benefit
• Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
• Mental Health & Family Forming Benefits
• Continuing education and corridor travel benefits
Our Connected Work Culture: Driving Innovation, Together
At Remitly, we believe that true innovation sparks when we come together. Our Connected Work Culture fosters dynamic in-person collaboration, where ideas ignite and challenging problems find solutions faster.
Under the Company's current hybrid-work expectations, employees in this position work onsite Tuesday through Thursday each week. Additional onsite attendance may be required based on business needs, and the Company may modify its hybrid-work expectations from time to time. These intentional in-office moments are vital for deepening relationships, fueling creativity, and ensuring your impact is felt where it matters most.
Remitly is an E-Verify Employer
At Remitly, we are dedicated to ensuring that our workplace offers equal employment opportunities to all employees and candidates, in full compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
Remitly is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Are you passionate about building AI-enabled products that help editors make better, faster, and more transparent decisions?
Do you enjoy working at the intersection of product strategy, scientific publishing, data science, and technology to deliver meaningful impact for global research communities?
About our team
Our team supports the editorial workflows of the largest scientific publisher in the world — millions of manuscript submissions a year, a portfolio of thousands of journals, and tens of thousands of editors. As submission volume grows, we modernise editorial processes, so they scale without compromising the integrity of the scientific record. We are a cross-functional, evidence-led team of engineers, UX, data scientists, product analysts and subject-matter experts, and we work to a simple standard: everything we do is grounded in user needs, and we use evidence to make commercially driven priority decisions.
About the role
This role owns a specific, high-value challenge: deep evaluation after peer review — the stage where an editor reads the reviewer reports and decides to accept, reject, or request revision, and ensure the manuscript reaches the publication standard. It is the most time-intensive stage in the workflow and the peak of editorial cognitive load and perceived editorial risk.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager with deep product judgement to own the strategy, vision and roadmap for editorial decision support at the post-peer-review stage. As a product manager for Elsevier’s global Submissions, you will enable growth of knowledge, research and innovation for our researcher community.
You will work within the wider publishing experience. You will help define the path from today’s manual workflow through system-guided support. You will work closely with an embedded data science team to commission and interpret evaluations of decision-support response accuracy, relevance and trust, and partner with the teams that own peer-review analytics and the wider Editor experience pipeline. We’re looking for a Product Manager who stays close to the technology and can reason about how the AI behaves, how it is evaluated, and where the trade-offs lie — while remaining, first and foremost, a product manager rather than an engineer or data scientists.
You will be part of a squad of engineers, UX, subject-matter experts and analysts to create a state-of-the-art user experience for article publication. Strong collaboration with stakeholders in Technology, Operations and Publishing will grow trust & build alignment. Creating solutions that are data-driven will contribute to our innovative culture for our digital submission products and services. You will inspire authors to return to Elsevier for the best experience from submission to trusted publication.
Role Responsibilities
• Owning, defining and driving the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for editorial decision-support solutions in the post-peer-review process.
• Leading delivery within a cross-functional agile team, managing priorities, maintaining a healthy backlog, and ensuring consistent product delivery.
• Partnering with scientific editors to understand decision-making challenges, gather user insights, and translate findings into impactful product improvements.
• Championing evidence-based decision-making through qualitative and quantitative research, analytics, experimentation, and clear success metrics.
• Collaborating with data science teams to evaluate AI-driven capabilities, including review synthesis, contradiction detection, and evidence linking, and using findings to prioritise enhancements.
• Measuring product success through business and user outcomes, defining KPIs and OKRs, communicating value, and assessing build, buy, or partner options.
• Working with engineering and technical teams to balance product, technical, and architectural considerations.
• Ensuring products support transparency, accountability, and responsible use of AI, with appropriate human oversight and auditability.
• Aligning stakeholders across Publishing, Technology, Operations, Editorial Strategy, and Research Integrity to build shared understanding and support.
• Supporting go-to-market activities, product launches, customer adoption, and migration planning.
Skills & Requirements:
• Significant product management experience, including ownership of product strategy, roadmap development, and delivery. Experience with Spec-Driven Development (SDD) is beneficial but not essential.
• Strong product judgment and the ability to define complex problems, evaluate trade-offs, and focus on user outcomes.
• Demonstrated experience working with AI and machine learning products, including generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), or agent-based workflows.
• Strong analytical skills and experience using data, experimentation, and research to inform decisions in uncertain or evolving environments.
• Experience leading product initiatives within cross-functional teams and delivering outcomes in complex settings.
• Experience collaborating with data scientists and translating model evaluations and insights into product decisions.
• An understanding of technical concepts and architectural trade-offs, with the ability to work effectively alongside engineering teams. Experience prototyping with AI tools is helpful but not required.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage technical and non-technical audiences.
• Commercial awareness and an understanding of how product decisions contribute to organisational goals and customer value.
• Familiarity with scholarly publishing, editorial workflows, peer review, or research integrity is advantageous but not required.
Work in a Way That Works for You
We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organisation. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals.
Working Pattern
Working flexible hours - flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive.
About the Business
A global leader in information and analytics, we help researchers and healthcare professionals’ advance science and improve health outcomes for the benefit of society. Building on our publishing heritage, we combine quality information and vast data sets with analytics to support visionary science and research, health education and interactive learning, as well as exceptional healthcare and clinical practice. At Elsevier, your work contributes to the world's grand challenges and a more sustainable future. We harness innovative technologies to support science and healthcare to partner for a better world.

Job Category:

All Job Posting Locations:
Beerse, Antwerp, Belgium, Leiden, Netherlands, Limerick, Ireland, Maidenhead, Berkshire, United Kingdom
Job Description:
About the Role
Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine is recruiting a Postdoctoral Researcher, AI Safety to join our Data, Data Science & AI organization. This is a fixed-term research appointment of two years reporting directly to the Scientific Fellow, AI Safety.
The role can be based at one of our sites in Belgium, The Netherlands, UK or Ireland
Agentic AI is becoming central to pharmaceutical R&D—from discovery and translational science to development and regulatory work—where evidence standards are rigorous and errors can ultimately affect patient safety and outcomes. Our GenAI Platform supports that shift across a rapidly expanding population of autonomous workflows. Safety at this scale cannot be retrofitted through checks written into individual applications; it must be a property of how these systems are built.
As a Postdoctoral Fellow, you will lead a focused, publishable research program on how agentic AI in pharmaceutical R&D can be governed through provable controls, continuously tested through adversarial assurance, and made safe by construction. Your research agenda will sit within one or more of the team's three connected mandates:
• Provable controls. Develop deterministic, explainable controls that persist throughout agentic workflows, and methods to verify that they hold.
• Adversarial assurance. Advance continuous red-teaming and evaluation methods that test safeguards against credible failure scenarios and produce defensible evidence.
• Safety-native architecture. Investigate pre- and post-training safety alignment and defense-in-depth techniques that make agentic AI safe by construction for regulated pharmaceutical R&D.
This is a hands-on research role with real systems as the testbed. You will formulate research questions, build the prototypes and experiments that answer them, publish the results, and work with our engineering partners to carry validated methods into the platform.
Key Responsibilities
Research Program
• Execute an independent research agenda (agreed with the Scientific Fellow/mentor) on controls, adversarial assurance, or safety-native architecture for agentic AI in regulated scientific settings.
• Design rigorous, reproducible experiments—including baselines, ablations, and uncertainty estimates—that test whether a safety property genuinely holds.
• Evaluate pre-training data interventions and post-training methods—including supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and safety tuning—for regulated scientific use cases, including whether safety properties persist under domain adaptation.
• Prototype layered architectures that constrain agent behavior, and translate scientific, quality, privacy, and regulatory requirements into testable system specifications.
• Work with platform engineering to move validated methods from prototype into the GenAI Platform, with documentation that makes results reproducible and auditable.
• Present your work to scientific, engineering, and leadership audiences, and represent the team at conferences, workshops, and standards activities.
What This Role Is Not
• Not frontier model development. We are not pre-training foundation models at scale. The research question is how alignment and architecture should be adapted so that the models and platforms available to us are safe for pharmaceutical R&D.
• Not a guardrail-prompt role. Safety here is architectural and enforcement is deterministic. A system prompt asking a model to behave is not a control.
• Not research in isolation. Your research questions come from real agentic workflows, and success includes evidence that the methods work on them—not only a publication.
• Not a production engineering or operations role. You prototype and validate; platform teams own production deployment, on-call support, and long-term maintenance.
Key Qualifications
PhD in computer science, AI/ML, applied mathematics, or a closely related technical field, preferably completed before the start date.
• A record of first-author research, evidenced by peer-reviewed publications or preprints, in AI safety/alignment, AI/ML for cybersecurity, formal methods, or a closely related area.
• Hands-on experience with foundation models and agentic AI, such as retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, planning, or multi-agent frameworks, and their failure modes.
• Strong programming skills (for example, Python and modern ML frameworks) and experience building reproducible experiments.
• Excellent written and verbal communication in English, with the ability to present technically defensible arguments to scientific and engineering audiences.
• Scientific rigor in characterizing model and agent behavior, including uncertainty, limitations, failure conditions, and the strength of supporting evidence.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with policy engines, authorization languages (for example, OPA/Rego or Cedar), or formal verification tools.
• Experience fine-tuning or evaluating foundation models for scientific or biomedical domains.
• Exposure to privacy-preserving ML, data de-identification, or data provenance, including their limitations.
• Interest in life sciences or another regulated, high-stakes domain
• Open-source contributions to AI safety, evaluation, or security tooling.

One week, you could be creating a campaign that changes how a client is viewed on a complex issue, connecting with policymakers, communities, and the public through compelling, data-driven stories and earned media. Account health and commercial growth. You'll manage accounts well - spotting and resolving issues related to budget, scope, and deliverables early on, turning challenges into opportunities. AI-enabled advice and delivery. Leading teams. You'll be a leader on the account teams you work across, setting the standard for the work, giving actionable feedback, sharing your experience to help colleagues and clients work through the hard problems, and building strong partnerships across the practice.

Building the firm. You'll lead and take part in pitches and proposals, spot opportunities to introduce FTI's wider services to clients, and represent the firm's values and standards, including a genuine commitment to the letter and the spirit of our code of conduct.

The judgement to advise senior stakeholders, up to and including boards and executive teams, and the presence to hold the room and stay calm when the stakes are high.

Excellent writing and the ability to make a sharp, credible case, whether in a boardroom or a pitch.

A practical, curious view on how AI is changing communications work, and a willingness to put it to use.

A collaborative approach and proven experience of working in an integrated way with multi-disciplinary teams

Direct experience across several TMT sub-sectors, for example software, telecoms, fintech, media, consumer tech or deep tech.

• Maintain documentation covering the CMDB data model, data sources, ownership, governance standards, reporting definitions, controls and operating procedures, and help users make effective use of ServiceNow data, reports and dashboards.

Simulation and Modelling Engineer - Graduate Programme 2027
Modelling modern weapon systems comes with many unique challenges. As a model developer, you will be working with highly sophisticated models, built up of multiple interdependent subsystems, to provide an accurate representation of the weapon system being used in real-world engagements. This means you'll often encounter new and exciting problems requiring your intuition and innovation to solve.
Salary: £31,900 plus a £3000 joining bonus
Dynamic working: The majority of your time you’ll be working onsite in an office environment with a team of people around you to support you with your work.
Security clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship.
Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team.
This role is scheduled to close for applications at midnight on Monday 2nd November 2026 but may close earlier depending on application volumes.
What we can offer you:
•
2 year Programme:  starting September 2027
•
Annual Salary Review
•
Company bonus: up to £2,500 (based on company performance and will vary year to year)
•
Pension: maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
•
Overtime: opportunity for paid overtime
•
Annual Leave:  25 days plus option to purchase extra holiday
•
Flexi Leave: up to 15 additional days
•
Excellent career progression and development opportunities
•
Facilities: fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
•
Healthcare Cash Plan: The Healthcare Cash Plan benefit provides the option to claim cash back on everyday healthcare expenses such as optical, dental, health and wellbeing and more.
The opportunity:
System modelling is a vital tool used to ensure MBDA provides reliable and cost effective weapon systems to our customers!
We build a variety of dynamic system performance models, embedded systems and real time models for MBDA products. Our models are developed and used extensively throughout the product lifecycle, from concept through to in service support. When used internally our performance models allow our system designers to estimate performance, which they can use to guide the product design. For our customer, performance models provide a method of verifying system performance whilst reducing reliance on prohibitively expensive testing and trials. Our real time models contribute to training environments for pilots and provide a variety of engineering testing capabilities. Once the product is in service, the customer continues to use our models to understand system capability and assist with operator training.
Models of modern weapon systems are made up of a large number of automated subsystems integrated together to provide the overall capability. This provides unique challenges when: developing accurate system - or system of system level - models that are both large in scale and highly sophisticated with many interdependencies; or when developing lower fidelity models designed to run at real time whilst maintaining an accurate representation of the weapon system. As a model developer this means you’ll often encounter new and exciting problems which will require you to apply your intuition and innovation to solve.
You’ll learn how to build simulation software in programming languages/environments such as:
•
Mathworks (MATLAB, Simulink and Stateflow)
•
Fortran
•
C/C++
Our teams implement Agile working practices and dynamic working across multiple projects to meet demand, aided by the use of collaborative tools. We also work closely with other departments and companies to integrate subsystem models and design data. From these interactions you’ll gain a broad understanding of each subsystem that makes up the weapon and how the system architecture makes these subsystems work together to provide an overall capability.
This role is best suited to those interested in mathematical modelling and programming, are passionate about solving complex problems within highly technical teams and enjoy working in a supportive environment.
What we’re looking for from you:
Degree qualified in Engineering (incl. General, Mechanical, Manufacturing / Production, Aeronautical/Aerospace, Software), Mathematics, Physics, Computing or Natural Science discipline to minimum 2:2
Our company: Peace is not a given, Freedom is not a given, Sovereignty is not a given
MBDA is a leading defence organisation.  We are proud of the role we play in supporting the Armed Forces who protect our nations. We partner with governments to work together towards a common goal, defending our freedom.
We are proud of our employee-led networks, examples include: Gender Equality, Pride, Menopause Matters, Parents and Carers, Armed Forces, Ethnic Diversity, Neurodiversity, Disability and more…
We recognise that everyone is unique, and we encourage you to speak to us should you require any advice, support or adjustments throughout our recruitment process.

About the FCA and team
We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK.
SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). As part of the Incident Response and Exercising team, you'll play a key role in coordinating the FCA's supervisory response to operational incidents affecting regulated firms, helping to protect consumers, maintain market confidence and support financial sector resilience.
Working within a collaborative and close-knit team, you'll partner with colleagues across the FCA and external stakeholders, including UK authorities, to minimise disruption and drive coordinated outcomes. You’ll contribute to and lead industry exercises, engage in domestic and international forums and support governance activities that boost operational resilience across the sector. You'll also help shape the FCA's understanding of emerging technologies, including AI and their impact on the evolving operational resilience landscape.
Role responsibilities
• Lead the FCA’s response to operational resilience incidents and cyber-attacks, helping to protect consumers, maintain market confidence and support the resilience of the UK financial system
• Coordinate timely incident triage and supervisory responses, enabling swift action to minimise disruption and potential consumer harm
• Work with other supervisory colleagues to develop effective incident response strategies that improve outcomes during critical events, including engaging with firms that are impacted by them
• Shape the FCA’s understanding of emerging technology risks, including AI, ensuring the organisation is prepared for evolving operational resilience challenges
• Coordinate alongside UK financial authorities during major incidents, contributing to a unified response where significant consumer or market impacts are at stake
• Empower supervision teams with specialist operational resilience expertise, enhancing their ability to assess risks, motivate firms and build up sector resilience
• Deliver critical insight, reporting and management information to senior leaders, supporting informed decision-making during high-profile incidents
• Champion best practice across the FCA as a trusted subject matter expert, providing guidance on incident reporting and operational resilience, building capability across teams and helping to create a safer, more resilient financial sector for millions of UK consumers
Skills required
Minimum:
• Prior experience in end-to-end operational incident and cyber incident management processes
• Prior experience with a well-developed analytical mindset and risk-based decision making in response to emerging crisis and urgent situations
• Prior experience of working in the financial sector
Essential:
• Experience across a range of technology and cyber resilience disciplines, bringing broad expertise to complex operational resilience challenges
• Knowledge of recognised resilience and risk management frameworks, such as COBIT, NIST or ITIL and their application to incident management and resilience practices
• Strong awareness of emerging technologies, including AI, cloud and automation, with the ability to assess their impact on operational resilience and incident response
• Ability to translate complex technology incidents into clear supervisory insights, considering consumer outcomes, market stability, firm resilience and wider sector dependencies
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present complex information clearly and confidently to a variety of internal and external audiences
• Proven ability to build effective relationships, work collaboratively across teams and engage credibly with diverse stakeholders
• Experience operating in fast-paced environments, responding to evolving incidents and providing clear, timely briefings and recommendations to senior decision-makers
Benefits

Your impact

• Trials activities

When a highly automated operation experiences a critical issue, every second counts. As a Technical Specialist at Dematic, you'll play a pivotal role in keeping a complex, fast-paced logistics operation running at peak performance. Working as part of a rotating day and night shift team, you'll act as the technical authority on shift, diagnosing complex faults, leading root-cause investigations and helping to prevent issues from recurring.
This is more than a maintenance role. You’ll combine hands-on technical expertise with leadership and coaching, helping to develop the capabilities of the wider engineering team while supporting one of the most advanced automated material handling environments in the industry.
If you're the person colleagues turn to when the difficult problems arise, and you enjoy sharing your knowledge as much as solving technical challenges, we'd love to hear from you.
We offer:
• Career Development
• Competitive Compensation and Benefits
• Pay Transparency
• Global Opportunities
Learn More Here:  https://www.dematic.com/en-us/about/careers/what-we-offer/
Tasks and Qualifications:
Key Accountabilities: As the technical lead on shift, you'll take ownership of complex automation and controls issues while ensuring the wider engineering team has the support and guidance needed to deliver exceptional performance.
• Acting as the primary technical escalation point for automation, controls and system performance issues.
• Diagnosing and resolving complex PLC, electrical, mechanical, electronic and network-related faults.
• Leading root-cause investigations and implementing permanent corrective and preventative actions.
• Using SCADA, WCS, WMS and operational data to identify trends, recurring failures and reliability improvement opportunities.
• Coordinating technical fault management between the customer, Dematic and specialist third-party support providers.
• Managing PLC backups, version control, software changes and technical documentation.
• Supporting planned maintenance activities and ensuring technical standards are maintained across the site.
• Driving continuous improvement initiatives that improve reliability, availability, performance and throughput.
• Supporting site performance by prioritising faults based on operational impact and business needs.
• Ensuring all work is carried out safely and in accordance with company and legislative requirements.
Helping Others Succeed: A key part of this role is developing the technical capability of the wider engineering team. We're looking for someone who enjoys sharing knowledge and helping others grow. You'll:
• Coach and mentor engineers through complex fault-finding activities.
• Provide technical support and guidance to shift technicians.
• Help develop technical training plans and skills-development programmes.
• Create and improve troubleshooting guides, technical documentation and best-practice processes.
• Support the ongoing development of the site's technical training matrix.
• Raise technical standards and confidence across the engineering team.
• Success in this role is measured not only by your own technical expertise, but also by your ability to elevate the capability of those around you.
The Technology You'll Work With: You'll work with a wide range of advanced automation technologies, including:
• Siemens PLC systems
• Industrial communication networks including Profinet, Profibus and AS-i
• SCADA and Equipment Information Systems
• Warehouse Control Systems (WCS)
• Warehouse Management Systems (WMS)
• Inverter drives and motion control technologies
• Barcode scanning and identification systems
• Automated conveyor and material handling equipment.
What We're Looking For: We're interested in engineers who enjoy understanding how complex systems work, thrive on solving technical challenges and take pride in developing others.
Essential
• HNC or equivalent qualification in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering.
• Strong PLC fault-finding and diagnostic experience.
• Experience within automated, manufacturing, production or logistics environments.
• Ability to interpret technical drawings, schematics and engineering documentation.
• Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Strong communication skills with the ability to provide technical leadership and guidance.
• A proactive approach to continuous improvement and root-cause analysis.
Desirable
• Siemens PLC experience.
• Recognised engineering apprenticeship.
• Experience working with automated warehouse or conveyor systems.
• Knowledge of SCADA, WCS or WMS platforms.
• Understanding of industrial communication networks.
• IOSH certification.
• Lean Six Sigma or continuous improvement experience.
• Experience working at height.

LOCATION: Belfast
GRADE: L3
TYPE: Full time

Airbus is embarking on one of its most critical industrial and supply chain integrations to date. As we absorb these manufacturing operations—a vital Tier 1 structures supplier—our objective is to integrate this complex aerostructure business into the core Airbus organization, while safeguarding the daily continuity of operations and global supply chain. Central to this monumental effort is the expansion of our Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system, replacing legacy tools with a unified SAP S/4HANA digital ecosystem.
In this context, a vacancy for a Logistics Transformation Product Owner (SAP S/4) in Belfast has arisen. The newly acquired Belfast site focuses on the A220 wings and A220 mid-fuselage components. As a Product Owner, you will strategically architect and drive the design & deployment of SAP S/4HANA.
HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE TEAM
• Drive the delivery of the Logistic team.
• Steer collaboration and alignment between Belfast Operations stakeholders (key users, executives), Process Owners and Information Management teams all along the project, from early discovery phase up to entry into service.
• Enable an efficient implementation of new processes and Airbus digital tools, aligned with SAP standards and Airbus global strategy.
• Perform in-depth analysis of current organization, processes and IT landscape.
• Assess and deliver the SAP S/4 HANA based solution. Collaborate with other Airbus S/4 projects to benefit from synergies and harmonize solutions.
• Deploy the SAP S/4 HANA solution together with the surrounding Airbus tool chain. Contribute to the deployment strategy elaboration. Perform business transformation. Ensure business adoption, especially via business acceptance tests. Prepare and execute data migration and entry into service. Orchestrate hypercare to support operations once deployment is done.
•  All along the project, focus on Logistic scope, while ensuring the integration with other domains (Finance, shopfloor, Planning & Supply, Manufacturing Engineering, Custom, Export Control).
• Manage the collaboration with other teams, inside and outside the Belfast project.

It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that sufficient detail is provided to demonstrate how they meet essential job criteria, as this alone will be used for vetting purposes.
Essential
• Be educated to degree level in Informatics, Logistic, Manufacturing Engineering,  Production or  Supply-chain, together with a minimum of  5 years’ relevant experience in Aerospace or related complex industries (e.g., Automotive, Defence) OR Be educated to HNC level in Informatics, Manufacturing Engineering,  Production or  Supply-chain, together with a minimum of  8 years’ relevant experience in Aerospace or related complex industries (e.g., Automotive, Defence).
• Qualified SAP/EWM and other SAP certifications are considered as a plus.
• Proven track record in performing change management.
• Mastery of project management
Desirable
• Logistic detailed knowledge. Global supply-chain end to end business understanding. Deep understanding of SAP supply-chain modules. S/4 proficiency, both in terms of solution and deployment methodology
• Knowledge of additional domains (on top of Logistic)  and experience in Logisitc Operations are a plus.
• Experience with SAFe/Agile frameworks.
• Previous experience in  SAP  transitions during corporate carve-ins/integrations is a distinct advantage.
Closing date: 5th of November 2026
Please note that meeting the mandatory criteria listed above guarantees consideration for the role, but does not ensure progression to the interview stage. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action. Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.

At Freshfields, our people are our greatest asset. We are a global law firm with an uncompromising commitment to excellence — and that commitment extends to how we invest in the careers of our people. This is a rare opportunity to play a genuinely influential role in the professional lives of talented lawyers, serving as a trusted, independent voice in a firm that takes career development seriously.
The Career Advisor role sits at the heart of our UK People function, providing personalised, confidential career coaching and advisory support to Associates across our London offices. If you are passionate about unlocking potential, skilled at building trusted relationships, and energised by the complexity of a world-class professional services environment, this role offers real breadth, purpose, and impact.
About the Role
Reporting to the Head of HR - UK&I, the Career Advisor acts as a dedicated and confidential resource for Associates navigating every stage of their careers at Freshfields. You will work collaboratively across the firm — partnering with Practice Group Leaders, HR Business Partners, the Diversity & Inclusion team, and Marketing and Business Development colleagues — to deliver against the firm's broader Talent Development strategy. You will also engage closely with Freshfields' global career development and coaching community, ensuring UK&I initiatives are aligned with and contribute to firmwide frameworks.
This is a role with genuine scope: from one-to-one coaching relationships to programme design, from data-driven insight to strategic stakeholder influence.
What You'll Do
Coaching and individual career support
You will provide high-quality, confidential career coaching to Associates on a wide range of topics — from practice integration and relationship building to performance improvement, promotion readiness, and long-term career planning. Engagements may range from targeted, short-term interventions to sustained advisory relationships, and you will support Associates through key transitions including progression to Senior Associate or Counsel, lateral moves, secondments, and return-to-work following parental or other leave.
Programme design and facilitation
You will design and deliver career development programmes and workshops that complement individual coaching and align with the firm's global learning and development offering. You will also oversee the UK mentoring programme, fostering effective mentor-mentee relationships and helping Associates develop, maintain, and review meaningful individual development plans.
Collaboration and stakeholder partnership
Working closely with HR Business Partners and Resource Managers, you will translate performance feedback into clear, actionable development plans and help Associates track progress against firmwide career frameworks. You will maintain strong relationships with partners, Marketing and Business Development, and the alumni network to surface external development opportunities, strategic secondments, and client-facing experiences. You will also partner with external coaching providers — in areas such as neurodiversity support, early careers coaching, and outplacement — ensuring quality and value.
Diversity, inclusion, and integration
You will work alongside the Diversity & Inclusion team to support the development and retention of a diverse Associate population and leadership pipeline, and will play an active role in embedding lateral hires quickly and effectively into the firm.
Insight and continuous improvement
You will use analytics and reporting to monitor the impact of coaching interventions, identify demographic and retention trends, and translate insight into engaging dashboards that demonstrate return on investment. Your observations will also feed into the broader Learning and Development agenda, helping to strengthen talent initiatives across the UK.
What We're Looking For
You will bring significant experience in professional development, coaching, or a career advisory capacity — ideally within a law firm or professional services environment — along with a genuine understanding of the legal profession and the career landscape within it. Specifically, we are looking for:
•
A bachelor's degree, and a coaching certification or equivalent (strongly preferred)
•
Demonstrable experience in a professional development, coaching, or career advisory role within a law firm, professional services firm, or academic institution; law firm practice experience is a strong advantage
•
Familiarity with legal career frameworks and the broader legal market
•
Exceptional judgement and discretion when handling sensitive and confidential information
•
The interpersonal skills and credibility to build trusted relationships across practice groups, seniority levels, and geographies — both in person and remotely
•
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt your style for diverse stakeholders
•
Strong analytical and organisational capability, with the confidence to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed environment
•
Proficiency in MS Office and HR systems, with the aptitude to learn new platforms quickly
Inclusion
Freshfields is an equal opportunities employer and all applications received by the firm will be considered on the basis of merit alone. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified individuals regardless of background. All offers of employment will be conditional on the candidate having or securing the right to work in the UK and providing the firm with evidence of that right (as required by the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006) prior to employment commencing.
Freshfields is a Ban the Box employer. We ask applicants to disclose criminal convictions only when a conditional job offer is made. A conviction does not automatically lead to withdrawal of the offer: we make decisions on a case-by-case basis and take a number of factors into account (for example, the role being applied for and the circumstances of the offence). You would have the opportunity to discuss the matter with us before we make a decision.
